newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brady bond father to bet on leading Latin debtor.
newsitem.headline: Brady bond father to bet on leading Latin debtor.

text.p: Nicholas Brady, the former U.S. Treasury chief whose bond plan helped rescue a number of bankrupt Latin American nations, said Thursday he was ready to invest in Brazil, one of the developing world's largest debtors.
"We have watched and waited and we think it's a good time to invest in Brazil," Brady told reporters at the outset of a two-day trip to eye business prospects.
Brady, who retired from the U.S. Treasury in 1993, oversaw the restructuring of billions of dollars in developing world debt into U.S.-backed Brady bonds.
He founded Darby Overseas Investments Ltd in 1994 to invest in promising mid-sized Latin American firms. Darby has $180 million in funds invested in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.
But so far Darby has avoided Brazil, one of the largest holders of restructured foreign debt with some $54 billion in Brady bonds.
"Investment opportunities in other countries came up earlier and (Brazil's economic stabilization plan) was put in later than all of the major Latin American countries," Brady said.
He added, however, that Brazil has made great strides on the inflation front over the past two years, which has provided a stable backdrop for steady economic growth.
Under the Brazilian government's stabilization program known as the Real Plan, monthly inflation rates have fallen from 50 percent to below one percent since the plan's inception in July 1994.

"We are looking to make investments with entrepreneurs and firms that are in the middle range, both privately held and publicly traded companies," Brady said, adding he was optimistic about increasing Darby's $180 million in funds under management.
Brady, who is Darby's chairman and chief executive officer, said he would visit Rio de Janeiro on Friday, where he would continue to hold private talks with Brazilian firms.
Brady spent 34 years as an investment banker before becoming U.S. Treasury Secretary in 1988 under former President Ronald Reagan.
